title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the heading on the previous page, 'Questions diverses en théorie de Tate-Hodge'. The setting is Tate's 1966 work on p-divisible groups. K is a p-adic field, C is the completion of its algebraic closure, π = Gal(K̄/K) and C(i) is the i-th Tate twist. The letter ℓ in the notes almost certainly equals p. For smooth proper X over K, Tate conjectured the Hodge-Tate decomposition H^n_et(X_K̄, Q_p) ⊗ C ≅ ⊕_{p+q=n} H^q(X, Ω^p) ⊗_K C(−p). Grothendieck lists open problems.

(a) Is there a de Rham-type comparison H_DR(X_C) ≅ H_Hdg(X_C)? He asks that it be functorial, multiplicative in X, commute with the structure homomorphisms, and respect the (generalized) filtrations of both sides, once a generator ε ∈ T_p(C*) = Z_p(1) is chosen. Here H_Hdg is the Hodge-Tate side (étale cohomology ⊗ C with its grading by twists). Choosing ε trivializes every C(i). The question is therefore whether étale and de Rham cohomology can be canonically compared over C, up to the choice of ε.

(b) Is every simple finite-dimensional Q_p[π]-module contained in some C(i)? A second question, partly illegible, asks whether such a module can contain (or be contained together as) both an M and an M(i) with i ≠ 0.

(c) Are there conditions on M = H^*(X_C, Z_p) ⊗ Q_p, as a Galois module, beyond those implied by Tate's (Hodge-Tate) conjecture? In other words: characterize the p-adic representations that come from geometry.

(d) Construct the Tate isomorphisms H^{pq}(X)_π ≅ H^q(X, Ω^p_X). Here the left side is (H^{p+q}_et ⊗ C(p))^π, the π-invariants.

(e) How do all these structures relate to canonical connections (Gauss-Manin connection, crystals)?

(f) How do they relate to Washnitzer-Monsky (formal/dagger) cohomology?

The page is thus a programme sheet for p-adic Hodge theory: comparison isomorphisms, the role of ε, characterization of geometric representations, and links with crystalline-type cohomologies.
errors: (b) as literally stated has a negative answer, by Tate's own results. V embeds in C(i) iff (V* ⊗ C(i))^π ≠ 0. For ψ = χ_cyc^a with a ∈ Z_p \ Z, Tate's theorem gives C(ψ^{-1}χ^i)^π = 0 for every integer i. So Q_p(ψ) lies in no C(i). Only representations with an integer Hodge-Tate (Sen) weight embed.

(a) cannot hold over C itself in a functorial, filtration-respecting way. Choosing ε identifies H_et ⊗ C with gr_F H_dR ⊗ C via Hodge-Tate. Passing to H_dR ⊗ C would require a functorial splitting of the Hodge filtration, which does not exist in general. The correct answer is Fontaine's: work over the filtered ring B_dR, where ε gives t = log[ε] and gr B_dR = ⊕ C(i). The question is well-motivated but the coefficient ring C is too small.

(b) second part: an irreducible M can embed in both C and C(i). Take M = V_p(E)^* for an elliptic curve E, which has Hodge-Tate weights 0 and 1. So the ?? question has a positive answer in easy examples.

ideas.what: Comparison isomorphism between de Rham cohomology and p-adic étale (Hodge-Tate) cohomology over C, compatible with filtrations, depending on a choice of ε ∈ T_p(C*)
ideas.modern_name: de Rham comparison theorem via B_dR (choice of ε giving t = log[ε])
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine (B_dR, ~1979-82; conjecture C_dR); proved by Faltings (1989), Tsuji, Scholze (2013)
ideas.where_published: Closely related to the 'mysterious functor' problem in Grothendieck's ICM Nice 1970 talk 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'

ideas.what: Which simple Q_p[Gal]-modules occur inside C(i)
ideas.modern_name: Hodge-Tate weights / Sen theory; C-admissible representations

ideas.what: Conditions on Galois representations from geometry beyond the Hodge-Tate property
ideas.modern_name: de Rham / potentially semistable representations; geometric representations (Fontaine-Mazur)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine (de Rham and semistable conditions), Fontaine-Mazur (1995), Berger (p-adic monodromy, 2002)

ideas.what: Construction of the Hodge-Tate isomorphisms (H_et ⊗ C(p))^π ≅ H^q(X, Ω^p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (conjecture 1967, abelian varieties with good reduction), Faltings (1988), Scholze

ideas.what: Link of Hodge-Tate structures with canonical connections and with Monsky-Washnitzer cohomology
ideas.modern_name: crystalline cohomology / Gauss-Manin connection / rigid cohomology and p-adic comparison (crystalline comparison)
ideas.where_published: Crystals: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968, in Dix exposés), ICM 1970

missed.claim: Grothendieck already ties a de Rham-étale comparison respecting filtrations to the choice of a generator ε of T_p(C*). This is exactly the datum Fontaine later used to build the period element t in B_dR. The page shows the role of ε was anticipated, though the ring C is too small.
missed.quote: compatible avec filtrations généralisées ... une fois donné un ε ∈ T_ℓ(C*) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical, not mathematical. It documents that the de Rham comparison problem, including its dependence on ε, was posed by Grothendieck around 1966-70, alongside the crystalline 'mysterious functor'.

missed.claim: Explicit question whether cohomology of varieties over p-adic fields satisfies conditions beyond Hodge-Tate. This is the local form of the 'which representations are geometric' problem, later answered by de Rham / potential semistability.
missed.quote: Y a-t-il d'autres conditions sur les M = H·(X_C, Z_ℓ) ⊗ Q_ℓ que celles résultant de la conjecture de Tate?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Settled (Fontaine, Faltings, Tsuji, Berger), but it is an early written formulation and could matter for attribution.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a programme page anticipating Fontaine's p-adic Hodge theory: a de Rham comparison depending on ε, the characterization of geometric representations, and links with crystals and Monsky-Washnitzer. Grothendieck's interest in these questions is already known through the 1970 'mysterious functor', and all the questions were later resolved. The explicit ε and the 'other conditions' question are mildly notable historical details.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Théorème de Rham [?]' is better read as 'Théorème de de Rham' (questions a) about a de Rham theorem).
'compatible avec filtrations {+généralisées+} des [?]': the illegible end is probably 'des deux membres'.
'Conditionner les remplissements [?] de Tate' should probably read 'Construire les isomorphismes de Tate'.
'Lien de ttes [?] ces structures' should read 'Lien de toutes ces structures'.
ℓ in 'T_ℓ(C*)', 'Q_ℓ(π)', 'Z_ℓ' should be understood as p (the residue characteristic) in this Tate-Hodge context.
The subscript B in H^{pq}_B(X)_π is uncertain in the image.
